title: Studying Cell Rolling Trajectories on Asymmetric Receptor Patterns
protocol: Fabricate microcontact printing polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) stamps with an inclination angle of α = 10° by an SU-8 molding process.
Clean the gold surface with piranha solution for 20 minutes and rinse it with DI water at 24.5 °C.
Ink the PDMS stamp with 5mM PEG solution in ethanol.
Dry the inked stamp in air for 20 minutes.
Gently place the stamp on the gold surface for 40 seconds to ensure good contact.
Rinse the surface with ethanol and dry it under a stream of N2.
Incubate the substrate within P-selectin solution (15 μg/mL in DPBS) using a perfusion chamber for 3 hours at 24.5°C.
Rinse the surface with copious DPBS to remove excess P-selectin.
Backfill the surface with BSA (1 mg/mL in DPBS) for 1 hour to block non-specific interactions.
Rinse the surface with copious DPBS.
Flow a suspension of HL60 cells (~10^5 cells/mL) over the patterned surfaces in a rectangular flow chamber at 24.5°C.
Generate a flow rate of 75 μL/min using a syringe pump.
Calculate shear stress using τ = 6μQ/wh², where μ is kinematic viscosity (0.001002 Pa s), Q is volumetric flow rate, w is width of the chamber, and h is height of the chamber.
Record HL60 cells rolling interactions with adhesive P-selectin substrates using an inverted microscope and a mounted camera at 1 frame per second for 300 seconds.
Perform three independent experiments for each shear stress magnitude and pattern inclination angle.
Analyze image sequences using a customized Matlab program.
Utilize particle tracking freeware to generate tracks along patterned line edges.
Select tracks extending till the end of a P-selectin band.
Fit selected tracks with two straight line segments aligned with flow and pattern edge.
Calculate edge tracking length from the segments.
Determine rolling velocity on the edge segment.
Determine rolling velocity on the plain region.
